newsitem.title: CANADA: CIBC tops off record quarter for Canada's banks.
newsitem.headline: CIBC tops off record quarter for Canada's banks.

text.p: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce on Thursday capped a record first-quarter performance for Canada's big six banks, reporting better-than-expected quarterly earnings.

Canada's second largest bank said earnings for the period ended Jan. 31 rose to a record C$375 million ($274 million) or C$1.71 ($1.25) a share from C$350 million ($255 million) or C$1.53 ($1.12) a share in the first quarter of 1996.

CIBC joined Canada's other big banks in topping analysts' earnings forecasts. According to a survey by Institutional Brokers Estimate Service (IBES), the average first-quarter earnings per share estimate for CIBC was C$1.63 ($1.19).
Analysts said the big banks' first-quarter earnings were a harbinger of higher profits for at least the rest of fiscal 1997 ending Oct. 31.

"We think they can maintain these levels of earnings and the rate of growth," said Hugh Brown, analyst at brokerage Nesbitt Burns, who said the banks' combined earnings rose by 14 percent in the first quarter.
Last year, Canada's big six banks topped the C$6 billion (US$4.4 billion) earnings mark, smashing the previous yearly profit record of C$5.2 billion (C$3.8 billion) in 1995.
Bank earnings are being driven by growing loan demand as the Canadian economy improves, and surging securities markets. Canada's banks own most of the country's securities industry.
CIBC said its problem loans fell sharply in the quarter to C$568 million ($415 million) from C$1.09 billion ($792 million) a year earlier.
Also on Thursday, CIBC said it planned to split its common stock two-for-one and issue at least 8 million preferred shares worth about $173 million, with an option to issue four million more.
CIBC shares soared C$1.65 to C$68.75 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday as bank shares extended their recent rally in Toronto.
